name: MATHVISTA
description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering diverse mathematical reasoning types, tasks, and visual contexts.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
inLanguage: English; also contains non-English questions including Chinese and Persian
rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was compiled from 31 source datasets: 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). The authors collected 9 multimodal MathQA datasets (2,666 examples) and reviewed more than 70 VQA datasets, selecting 19 publicly available datasets containing math-related instances. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, followed by manual labeling by three expert annotators and majority voting, resulting in 2,739 examples. The three new datasets were introduced to cover logical reasoning on puzzle test diagrams, algebraic reasoning on functional plots, and scientific reasoning on academic figures, totaling 736 newly curated questions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data come from 31 source datasets, including 9 existing MathQA datasets, 19 existing VQA datasets, and 3 newly created datasets: IQTest sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, FunctionQA emphasizing functional plots, and PaperQA sourced from informative academic illustrations including tables, figures, and charts from online education resources, with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA includes 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation in the final benchmark. For VQA datasets, heuristic filtering selected examples with numeric answers or quantity words in questions, followed by manual verification and majority voting. For release, the dataset was split into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) using a sampling strategy that first randomly sampled questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset and then sampled remaining questions proportionally to dataset size.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, the authors designed heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or quantity words in the questions were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples, after which three expert annotators manually labeled whether they involved mathematical reasoning. The authors also conducted several quality checks to address unidentified errors.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills. For the 19 VQA datasets, three expert annotators manually labeled whether filtered examples involved mathematical reasoning, using instructions and an annotation tool with options Yes, No, and Unsure; majority voting was used. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a two-step review process in which each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers and disagreements were resolved through discussion. Mathematical reasoning categories were coarsely labeled automatically from source dataset details, and expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven reasoning candidates to verify automatic annotation quality.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom annotation tool/GUI developed by the authors; Amazon Mechanical Turk was used for human performance baseline and Bard assessment tasks.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the newly collected 736 questions, independent annotation by three reviewers resulted in a 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate, with only 6 disagreements resolved through discussion. For labeling whether VQA examples involved mathematical reasoning, inter-annotator agreement among three annotators had a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775. For mathematical reasoning category verification, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 for manual labeling of mathematical reasoning involvement in VQA examples; 3 for annotation of newly collected datasets; 5 for human performance evaluation on testmini
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; expert annotators; Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators with more than 5,000 HIT tasks completed, acceptance score higher than 0.99, and high school diploma or higher for the human performance study
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules for selecting math-related VQA examples; automatic annotation from source dataset details for coarse mathematical reasoning labels; GPT-4-based answer extractor; EasyOCR; Multimodal Bard for caption generation
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and the authors will maintain an online evaluation platform. The benchmark is described as part of an ongoing research process, with commitments to maintaining the datasets by refining potential data noise in response to community feedback and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language; grade level; educational attainment of human annotators
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to facilitate development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluate progress of LLMs and LMMs toward general-purpose AI assistants capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks. The paper highlights applications in education, statistical analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that source datasets are heterogeneous and annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations and lacking a unified format and structure. It also notes possible gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. For VQA filtering, heuristic selection initially produced some false positives.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may have gaps in coverage of certain mathematical problems and visual contexts. Collecting high-quality data is labor-intensive, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and due to heterogeneous sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models. The paper also notes that answer labels for the test set are not publicly released to prevent data contamination.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of foundation models for mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. The dataset is divided into testmini for model development validation or limited computing resources and test for standard evaluation. The benchmark supports deterministic evaluation using accuracy on multiple-choice and free-form numerical answers.
